newsitem.title: FINLAND: TRENDLESS HELSINKI ENDS LOWER WITH OVERSEAS.
newsitem.headline: TRENDLESS HELSINKI ENDS LOWER WITH OVERSEAS.

text.p: * Shares end listless session down in line with trend overseas.
Investors sidelined ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve FOMC meeeting
where no rate changes expected. Metsa-Serla down on Swiss Biber
acquisition. Volume fair 380 mln markka, 24 pct in Nokia.
Shares slipped in trendless
trade on Tuesday, taking their cue from Wall Street's early fall
on uncertainty ahead of news from the Federal Reserve's policy
setting meeting due at 1915 GMT, brokers said.
Nokia closed at at 246.00, down 8.50 markka or 3.3 percent,
reflecting Wall Street's volatility.
"All this volatility is putting people off," said one.
Strong November U.S. housing starts knocked the bond market
lower in the afternoon and spread woes around the stock market
as well, brokers said.
The market outlook depended on what the outcome of the Fed
meeting which was not expected to move rates amid signs that the
U.S. economy is settling down as the year draws to a close.
Forest industry group Metsa-Serla fell 0.70 markka or two
percent to close at 32.00 markka on its acquisition of part of
troubled Swiss Biber Holding AG, brokers said.
It bought troubled Biber's fine paper business Biberist,
with annual net sales of around 1.5 billion markka, for less
than 300 million markka, which analysts found cheap -- but many
voiced concern at Metsa-Serla's acquisitiveness.
